data.title: Greeks.Live Researcher: Bitcoin and Ether in Deep Negative Gamma Zone, Hedging May Amplify Volatility
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing CoinDesk, data from options platform Greeks.Live show that Bitcoin and Ether are in negative gamma territory, where market makers’ routine hedging may amplify price swings. To stay directionally neutral, market makers typically hedge by trading tokens or futures; in a negative gamma environment, they may need to sell as prices fall and buy as prices rise, reinforcing market moves.

Greeks.Live macro researcher Adam said both assets have entered deep negative gamma territory. Bitcoin is in negative gamma across roughly $58,000 to $72,000, with little positive gamma support below its current price, according to the chart. Such hedging could trigger a chain reaction in which a modest decline leads to large-scale liquidations in perpetual futures. Adam said order books may remain fragile and price action momentum-driven until BTC and ETH return to the gamma-flip level of about $73,000.

data.title: Richard Haass Says Nvidia Shakeup Has National Security Implications
data.description:
Centerview Partners Senior Counselor Richard Haass said the national security implications of the Nvidia shakeup extend beyond the company, according to Bloomberg.

The comments came at the end of a week that saw revelations of ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged affairs with employees and a suspected Chinese spy.

data.title: Harley Lewis Foote Says Malicious WhatsApp Attack Left Him With $800
data.description: Trader Harley Lewis Foote said a malicious WhatsApp payload gave attackers full remote access to his computer and allegedly downloaded without a click. According to Odaily, the attackers waited five days while monitoring Foote’s publicly disclosed short position, then closed it as Bitcoin approached $68,000. Foote said the hackers moved his funds through Hyperliquid, MetaMask and Tornado Cash, leaving him with $800. They also allegedly accessed his email, passwords, website and X account. Foote said the attackers had tested a $10 withdrawal to avoid attracting attention. He said all his dollar funds except the $800 were taken, and that the loss involved years of savings and work.

data.title: Bank of England's Megan Greene: Acting Now on Inflation Can Minimize Policy Mistakes
data.description:
Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee member Megan Greene said on Saturday that acting proactively on inflation now, rather than being overly cautious and risking severe second-round effects, would help minimize the downside of policy mistakes. According to Sina Finance, Greene said at a Centre for European Reform conference that when the path of inflation is uncertain, policymakers should consider how to minimize the harm caused by decision errors.

At the Bank of England's November meeting, Greene was among the MPC majority who voted to raise borrowing costs from 3.75% to 4%; she had previously been among a minority calling for earlier rate hikes. She reiterated that, given uncertainty about the inflation outlook, the risk of raising rates too much and then cutting them if second-round effects do not emerge was much smaller than the risk of waiting too long to tighten and allowing inflation to get out of control. Greene said inflation had remained above target for about five and a half years, and failing to bring it under control now would be a greater risk and a more serious policy mistake.

data.title: Binance Market Update | Bitcoin Hits $67K: Is Anthropic’s IPO Draining Crypto?
data.description: Bitcoin is down 20%+ since October, its lowest since August, and analysts are split on why. Some blame investors raising cash for Anthropic’s 6x-oversubscribed IPO; others see a wider AI-trade unwind. Under 45% of active supply is in profit, a zone that has often marked correction lows. Tap for the full breakdown.Bitcoin Falls to $68,000 as Analysts Split on Whether Anthropic’s 6x-Oversubscribed IPO Is Draining CryptoBitcoin fell to around $68,000 overnight, its lowest since August, and was last near $67,240, extending a slide of more than 20% since early October. Anthropic’s IPO, which could raise up to $64.4B, is about six times oversubscribed, per Bloomberg. Xapo Bank CEO Seamus Rocca said order books opening pull money from liquid assets like bitcoin as investors scramble for allocations, and compared it to SpaceX’s IPO, which he said temporarily drained money from bitcoin. Risk Dimensions’ Mark Connors sees a wholesale deleveraging of the AI trade, citing gold’s decline. Hyperium Decimus’ Chris Sullivan sees no logical link between Nvidia’s troubles and bitcoin, pointing instead to shorts above their August peak, large IBIT outflows, extreme fear and the chance of a 50bp Fed hike within 30 days. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s exit (shares fell as much as 14% on November 12) and Strategy’s MSCI removal at the November 30 close added pressure, though Schwab’s Jim Ferraioli said the timing of the sharpest drop, around 11 p.m. Eastern, suggests neither was the direct trigger. Strive CEO Matt Cole notes bitcoin fell 19% in the 50 days before SpaceX listed versus 18% before Anthropic; after SpaceX it bottomed 18 days later and was 28% higher by day 100. A repeat would put bitcoin near $90,000 by late February, though Strategy-related selling concerns also played a role then. Global Stock Funds Draw $98 Billion in a Week, Second-Largest Inflow Ever, as Investors Buy the DipGlobal equity funds took in a net $98B in the week to November 14, the second-largest weekly inflow on record and the fifth straight week of inflows, totaling about $350B. The four-week average rose to about $75B, a record; at the 2021 meme-stock peak it reached only about $45B. Global tech funds drew $2.6B in the week and $9.1B over three weeks despite the selloff. US spot bitcoin ETFs have swung to $1.56B in net outflows for 2026.Most Active Bitcoin Supply Now Held at a Loss as Share in Profit Drops Below 45%Less than 45% of bitcoin’s active supply is held at a profit, excluding coins unmoved for more than 10 years. Readings below 40% have often coincided with lows of market corrections, while readings near 100% have tended to raise reversal risk. Some investors use this as a contrarian signal. Bitcoin trades near $67,000, its lowest since August.Morgan Stanley’s Bitcoin ETF Adds 735 BTC This Week, Lifting Holdings to 11,625 BTC; Its Solana ETF Moves 24,452 SOLMSBT added about 735 BTC (about $52.87M) this week, per Arkham, bringing holdings to 11,625 BTC, worth about $784M, while US spot bitcoin ETFs overall saw heavy outflows. It took in $20M on November 10 as other funds lost money. Separately, Morgan Stanley’s Solana ETF (MSOL) moved 24,452 SOL to an exchange address Saturday morning, possibly to sell.Nvidia Says No CEO Talks Underway as "Stand With Jensen" Petition Tops 77,900 SignaturesNvidia says it is still selecting a search firm and has “not formally engaged with any potential candidates,” calling speculation premature, per Bloomberg. This followed an FT report that the board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas; Arm fell nearly 10% Friday before paring losses. Nvidia cut ties with Huang on Thursday over a scandal involving extramarital affairs and reports he was targeted by a suspected Chinese spy. A petition to reinstate him has more than 77,900 signatures, over 41,900 self-identified shareholders and 5,200 current or former employees, alleging removal “without meaningful due process.” Elon Musk signed and is lead signatory; Marc Andreessen and Garry Tan are also listed. The site notes all identities are self-reported and unverified.

data.title: Global Stock Funds Draw $98 Billion in a Week, Second-Largest Inflow Ever, as Investors Buy the Dip
data.description: Global equity funds took in a net $98 billion in the week to November 14, the second-largest weekly inflow on record, according to fund flow data. It was the fifth straight week of inflows, bringing the total to about $350 billion.The four-week average of inflows rose to about $75 billion, a record high. At the peak of the 2021 meme-stock frenzy, the four-week average reached only about $45 billion.Technology funds also drew money despite the recent tech selloff. Global tech equity funds took in a net $2.6 billion during the week and $9.1 billion over the past three weeks.The flows into stocks contrast with crypto. US spot bitcoin ETFs have swung to $1.56 billion in net outflows for 2026, after heavy withdrawals over the past two weeks.

data.title: Bitcoin News | Most Active Bitcoin Supply Now Held at a Loss as Share in Profit Drops Below 45%
data.description: Less than 45% of bitcoin’s active supply is now held at a profit, meaning most actively held coins are currently worth less than their holders paid, according to on-chain data. The estimate excludes coins that have not moved in more than 10 years, many of which are considered lost or illiquid.Historically, readings below 40% have often coincided with the lows of market corrections. When the share in profit nears 100%, the risk of a market reversal has tended to rise.Some investors use this pattern as a contrarian signal, adding to positions when losses dominate and reducing them when most holders are in profit.The data comes as bitcoin trades near $67,000, its lowest since August.

data.title: Kava Says Abnormal Cross-Chain Activity Was Controlled and Limited to Kava Lend, Not Unlimited Minting

Partner trading platforms paused related deposits and withdrawals as a routine precaution. Kava said it would provide more details as soon as possible.

data.title: Developer Track Offers $10,000 in Cash Prizes for Top Three Places
data.description:
BNB Chain announced on X that the Developer Track will offer $10,000 in cash prizes across its top three places. First place is set to receive $5,000, second place $3,000 and third place $2,000. The post separately says top teams from both tracks can access an EASY Residency fast-track and potential investment through the $1 billion Builder Fund. The cash-prize breakdown is specifically for the Developer Track, while the fast-track and potential investment opportunities are described as available to top teams from both tracks.

The announcement presents investment as a possibility, not a guaranteed outcome. BNB Chain explicitly stated that investment through the Builder Fund is not guaranteed, and the post does not say that every top team will receive funding. It also does not provide further details about the selection process, eligibility criteria, track requirements or the terms of the residency fast-track. The listed prizes total $10,000: $5,000 for first place, $3,000 for second place and $2,000 for third.

data.title: Helius Launches Beta Historical Accounts API for Querying Account States at Any Point
data.description: Solana RPC provider Helius has launched the beta version of its Historical Accounts API. According to Odaily, the API can retrieve the complete state of any account, liquidity pool or wallet at the end of a specified slot or after a transaction executes. It can be used to backtest trading strategies, check historical token supply, calculate PnL, retrieve past wallet balances and track changes in DEX liquidity over time.

data.title: Bitcoin News | Bitcoin Falls to $68,000 as Analysts Split on Whether Anthropic’s 6x-Oversubscribed IPO Is Draining Crypto
data.description: Bitcoin fell to around $68,000 overnight, its lowest since August, extending a slide of more than 20% since early October as a series of market shocks weighed on crypto. It was last trading near $67,240.Analysts disagree on what’s driving the latest drop. Some point to investors raising cash for Anthropic’s IPO, while others see a broader move out of riskier assets.Anthropic IPO Draws Six Times More Orders Than SharesAnthropic’s IPO, which could raise up to $64.4 billion, is about six times oversubscribed, Bloomberg reported. That means investors have placed orders for six times as many shares as are on offer.Seamus Rocca, CEO of Xapo Bank, said the opening of the order books is pulling money out of liquid markets as investors scramble for an allocation. “When an IPO of this scale comes to market, the lure of a quick return is strong, and liquid assets like bitcoin are often the first source of funding when investors scramble for allocations,” he said.Rocca called it set to be “the largest public listing in history, by a wide margin.” On its own, the IPO would raise less than SpaceX’s $75 billion listing in June. It would be larger only when combined with Anthropic’s separate $26 billion private placement, or if the deal is increased.Rocca compared the rush to SpaceX’s IPO, which he said temporarily drained money from bitcoin. He added that bitcoin has held up relatively well given the amount of bad news markets have absorbed.Other Analysts See Broad Risk-CuttingOther analysts see the drop as part of a market-wide retreat from risk rather than anything specific to bitcoin.“Gold’s decline shows me it is a wholesale derisking deleveraging of the AI trade,” said Mark Connors, chief investment strategist at Risk Dimensions.Chris Sullivan, co-portfolio manager at Hyperium Decimus, said he sees “no logical connection” between Nvidia’s troubles and bitcoin. Instead, he pointed to:Short positions in bitcoin above their August peakLarge outflows from BlackRock’s IBITExtreme fear in crypto marketsThe chance of a 50 basis point Fed rate hike within the next 30 days“Metals are trading lower with crypto, which is again pretty insane,” Sullivan said.Nvidia CEO Exit and Strategy’s MSCI Removal Add PressureSeveral other events have weighed on sentiment:Nvidia: CEO Jensen Huang resigned on November 12, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO. Nvidia shares fell as much as 14% that day, hitting the wider AI trade.Strategy: MSCI is removing Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, from its USA Index at the close of November 30 under new rules for non-operating companies. That could force index-tracking funds to sell its shares.Jim Ferraioli, head of crypto research at the Schwab Center for Financial Research, said the timing of bitcoin’s sharpest drop, around 11 p.m. Eastern, suggests neither event was the direct trigger.SpaceX IPO Pattern Points to $90,000, One Analyst SaysStrive CEO Matt Cole sees parallels with SpaceX’s IPO. Bitcoin fell 19% in the 50 days before SpaceX listed, compared with 18% over the same period ahead of Anthropic’s planned debut.After SpaceX went public, bitcoin kept falling and hit a low 18 days later, then recovered. By day 100 it was 28% above its level on the listing day. “If Anthropic follows the same pattern, most of the drawdown is behind us, and it could reverse quickly over the next couple of months,” Cole said. A repeat would put bitcoin near $90,000 by late February, he said.The comparison has limits. Bitcoin’s drop around the SpaceX IPO also came with concerns about bitcoin sales by Strategy, so the IPO wasn’t the only factor.
